title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this first draft of 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck tries to axiomatize a tame ('modérée') geometry of figures in a space X, such as polyhedral or semi-algebraic sets. He wants to do this purely combinatorially, from a set F_él of 'elementary figures' (convex cells, the 'ingrédients' of p. 9).

The structure on F_él so far:
- an order ≤, meaning inclusion of figures;
- a reflexive, symmetric 'compatibility' relation R (p. 7);
- a 'configuration' is a set of pairwise compatible elementary figures (p. 7).

On this page, to an arbitrary figure F he attaches Φ = Σ'_F ⊂ F_él, the set of elementary figures associated with (contained in) F. He states three properties:
- (a) Φ is closed in the ordered set F_él. Most naturally this means down-closed, i.e. closed for the Alexandrov topology: if F0 ≤ F1 ∈ Φ then F0 ∈ Φ.
- (b) Any two distinct elements of Φ are compatible, so Φ is a configuration. This is consistent with the NB on p. 7: two elementary figures lying in a common figure are compatible.
- (c) Φ is 'locally finite' in a suitable sense.

To allow infinite (non-compact) figures, one singles out in P(F_él) the locally finite subsets, those whose family of supports in X is locally finite. These form an 'antifiltre', i.e. an ideal of the Boolean algebra P(F_él): stable under subsets and finite unions. Page 9 makes this explicit as axiom ④ with sub-axioms a)–d).

Converse claim: every Φ satisfying (a)(b)(c) comes from one and only one figure.

So figures are encoded as locally finite, down-closed, pairwise-compatible subsets of a poset carrying a compatibility relation. This is a first step towards an abstract, axiomatic 'analysis situs' independent of a point-set topology. On p. 9 the data (F_él, ≤, R, locally finite configurations) are listed as the resulting structure.
errors: The bijection 'toute Φ satisfaisant a) b) c) provient d'une figure et d'une seule' is not correct if 'fermée' only means down-closed. Take Φ generated by two adjacent cells. The figure F = their union contains further elementary figures, e.g. a convex cell straddling both, which are not in Φ. So Σ'_F ≠ Φ, and distinct Φ give the same F: injectivity of Φ ↦ F fails.

To repair this, (a) must be a saturation condition: every elementary figure contained in a finite union of members of Φ lies in Φ. Alternatively one passes to equivalence classes of Φ. Grothendieck may intend 'fermée' in this stronger sense, but it is not stated.
Condition (c) is left vague ('en un sens convenable'). It is only partially made precise on p. 9.

ideas.what: Encoding a figure by its set of elementary subfigures: a down-closed, pairwise-compatible, locally finite subset of a poset with compatibility relation
ideas.modern_name: cell/face posets of polyhedral or semialgebraic complexes; down-sets in the Alexandrov topology; cliques in a coherence space
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology for complexes; tame topology / o-minimality (van den Dries, Shiota) for tame geometry
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is programmatically announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5, but this axiomatics is not developed there

ideas.what: Locally finite subsets forming an 'antifiltre' (ideal of P(F_él)) as a bornology-like structure
ideas.modern_name: ideal of subsets / bornology; locally finite families

ideas.what: 'Configuration' = set of pairwise compatible elements of an ordered set with a symmetric reflexive relation
ideas.modern_name: configurations of prime event structures (Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel 1981); cliques of coherence spaces (Girard 1987)

missed.claim: The data (F_él, ≤, compatibility R, locally finite configurations, figures = down-closed pairwise-compatible locally finite sets) are formally almost identical to prime event structures: events with causality order and conflict, configurations as left-closed conflict-free sets, and a finiteness axiom. Grothendieck even uses the same word 'configuration'. Geometric realization of such structures links to Pratt's higher-dimensional automata and directed topology. The analogy between tame geometric figures and event structures / coherence spaces is not drawn in the literature as far as I know.
missed.quote: Si F_1, F_2 ∈ Φ, F_1 ≠ F_2, alors F_1, F_2 sont compatibles, i.e. Φ est une configuration
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could suggest a concurrency-theoretic / domain-theoretic reading of tame topology, where figures are elements of a domain of configurations. It is likely a structural coincidence of limited depth.

missed.claim: This is an attempt at a purely combinatorial (point-free) axiomatics of tame figures via elementary cells, compatibility and local finiteness, developed over pp. 7–9. It is never completed in published form.
missed.quote: Inversement, toute Φ satisfaisant a) b) c) provient d'une figure et d'une seule.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to point-free approaches to o-minimal or tame topology. Note, however, that the reconstruction theorem needs a saturation hypothesis.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, somewhat naive draft of a combinatorial axiomatics for tame topology, and it contains a gap in the uniqueness claim. It is of interest as unpublished material on Esquisse §5 themes and for its coincidental match with event-structure 'configurations'. Mathematically it is mostly routine.
transcription_corrections: '$\mathcal{F}il$' (four times) should be read as '$\mathcal{F}_{\acute{e}l}$', the set of elementary figures, as on pp. 7 and 9.

The sentence beginning 'Dans le cas où on veut exclure' is likely 'Dans le cas où on ne veut [pas] exclure le cas des figures infinies'. Logically the local-finiteness ideal is needed precisely when infinite figures are allowed. The handwriting looks like 'D__ si on ne veut exclure les cas des figures infinies'.
'satisfaisant' is written 'satisfaisant' in the image, abbreviated 's.tisfaisant'.
